title: Surface composition and typography rescale for accessible compact mode
creator: Asha Mendel
description: Consolidate token deltas and rescale typography specifically for the compact (high-density) mode used in tables, lists, and control surfaces. Goal is to establish a deterministic surface composition matrix (color ramps + elevation steps) and a proportional typography scale that preserves contrast and legibility at small sizes while preventing visual churn across component states. This ticket scopes the token decisions, spec updates, and handoff artifacts required for implementation across Buttons, DataTable rows, Form controls, and Chart legends.
acceptance_criteria: A single compact-mode token palette is defined and documented (semantic color tokens, 4-step elevation, 3 radius sizes) and approved by Design and Accessibility.
Typography scale for compact mode (xs, sm, base) with line-height and tracking values that meet AA contrast/legibility at target sizes is published to the token repo.
A reference implementation exists in the component library for Button (primary/secondary/ghost), DataTable row/striping, and Legend items with visual regression snapshots passing thresholds.
A migration guide for teams is provided describing delta mapping from legacy tokens and recommended quick-fixes for older screens.
Telemetry instrumentation hooks added to report percentile font-size / truncation regressions for one release cycle.
work_notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after design ops audit highlighted incoherent compact tokens across widgets. Identified priority surfaces: table rows, compact buttons, and chart legends.

2026-02-25: Exploratory mocks created — three candidate approaches for compact typography: proportionally scaled fluid, fixed stepped scale, and condensed spacing with retained x-height. Outcome: stepped scale preferred for predictability.
2026-02-28: Accessibility review (internal) recommends minimum font-size 12px for interactive labels; when 11px unavoidable, increase tracking by +6 and raise contrast by 3% on semantic surface.

2026-03-03: Prototype components implemented in branch design/compact-tokens (GitHub: GH-PR-4487). Early visual diff shows data table row density improved, but ghost button hit area reduced — added implementation note to keep touch target >= 36px.

2026-03-07: Cross-team sync with Engineering and PM. Eng raised concerns about legacy CSS overrides and token naming collisions in packages; agreed to provide a mapping table and feature-flagged rollout.
2026-03-10: Design review meeting — design lead approved color ramp and elevation steps. Preparing final spec and handoff docs for implementation phase.
decisions: Adopt a ‘compact-mode’ semantic token namespace (e.g., surface.compact.*) instead of overloading existing tokens — reduces breaking changes for teams.
Use a 4-step elevation ladder for compact surfaces with smaller shadow spread but preserved relative depth to maintain affordance cues.
Typography will use a 3-step compact scale (compact-xs, compact-sm, compact-base) with explicit letter-spacing deltas and line-height values; no condensed typeface substitution.
Button touch targets will retain minimum sized tappable area via internal padding overrides even when visual density is reduced.
risks: Teams might opt out of compact tokens and keep legacy styles, causing inconsistent UI density across product — mitigation: migration guide + lint rule to flag legacy tokens.
Smaller elevations can reduce perceived clickability on low-contrast displays — mitigation: increase subtle border or micro-gradient on call-to-action surfaces where needed.
Edge-case: chart legends with very long labels may still truncate; recommend hotfix patterns (wrap + tooltip) documented in component guide.
Implementation risk: monorepo token import order could cause cascade overrides; include QA checklist and unit tests for token resolution.
